optionReasons.saa-ini-018:option:0: Internet Gateway connects to VPC to INTERNET — the requirement is precisely to avoid the internet.
optionReasons.saa-ini-018:option:2: NAT Gateway redundant continues to route over the internet and costs per hour + per GB.
optionReasons.saa-ini-018:option:3: VPC Peering connects VPCs to each other — S3/DynamoDB are not VPCs.

finalJustifications: Because the Gateway Endpoint (exclusive for S3 and DynamoDB) adds private route in the route table: access through the internal network of the AWS, without internet, without NAT and no cost.
Because Gateway Endpoint creates a local cache of S3 within the VPC, serving the objects without repeating the trip to the pocket.
Because Gateway Endpoint assigns temporary public IPs to private entities during calls to the APIs of the S3 and DynamoDB.
Because the Gateway Endpoint charges for GB processed, but much less than the NAT Gateway — the economy comes from the reduced rate.

optionReasons.saa-ini-019:option:0: The CloudFront distributes content publicly by edge — does not expose service PRIVADO between VPCs.
optionReasons.saa-ini-019:option:1: Internet Gateway involves public Internet traffic — what is to be avoided.
optionReasons.saa-ini-019:option:2: Direct Connect link datacenters ON-PREMISES to AWS — is not the private consumption mechanism between VPCs.

finalJustifications: Because PrivateLink publishes the service behind a NLB and customers consume it by endpoints interface with private IPs on their VPCs — without internet and without peering.
Because PrivateLink creates an automatic peering among all VPC clients, unifying networks in a routing domain only.
Because PrivateLink exposes the service by a VPN site-to-site managed, with dedicated tunnels for each consumer customer.
Because PrivateLink replicates the service within the VPC of each customer, performing a local copy isolated by consumer.

optionReasons.saa-ini-020:option:1: The entry is NOT allowed by default — without entry rules, every inbound is denied.
optionReasons.saa-ini-020:option:2: No door is released by default — nor SSH.
optionReasons.saa-ini-020:option:3: The exit is released by default — 'all denied' is wrong in the half outbound.

finalJustifications: Because one Security Group new has no entry rules (imply negates all inbound) and has a standard rule releasing all exit traffic.
Because Security Group new automatically inherits the default group rules from VPC until you receive your own.
Because Security Group new block also the exit until the first rule is created, isolating the instance completely.
Because Security Group new allows only entry of instances of the same VPC, the implicit perimeter of confidence.

optionReasons.saa-ini-021:option:0: The Internet Gateway is the connectivity component of VPC — is not an administrative access point.
optionReasons.saa-ini-021:option:2: The NAT Gateway allows private entities to exit — no administrator entry.
optionReasons.saa-ini-021:option:3: The ELB Distribute application traffic — does not concentrate access SSH Administrative.

finalJustifications: Because the bastion host is the hardened instance in the public sub-network that concentrates access SSH/RDP to private bodies — single controlled entry point.
Because the bastion host hides the IP of private entities via NAT, translating addresses to each access session.
Because the bastion host authenticates the administrators instead of the IAM, with a local key directory SSH authorized.
Because the bastion host replicates the commands SSH for all private entities, administering the entire fleet at once.

optionReasons.saa-ini-022:option:0: IGW + Public IPs EXPOSURE instances to input connections — violates central requirement.
optionReasons.saa-ini-022:option:1: Peering connects VPCs — doesn't give internet access to private sub-networks.
optionReasons.saa-ini-022:option:2: The WAF filter requirements in ALB/CloudFront/API Gateway — Does Not Provide Exit Path.

finalJustifications: Because NAT Gateway in the public sub-network (referenced on the private route) allows exit connections (patches) and blocks any connection started from outside.
Because NAT Gateway scans downloaded packages for malware, the required filter for security patches.
Because NAT Gateway Open the door. 443 entry only for the servers of the AWS, secure channel of two patches.
Because NAT Gateway lowers updates once and distributes them internally to sub-network instances.

optionReasons.saa-ini-033:option:0: The CloudTrail REGISTRA calls from API — is the data source, not the smart detector.
optionReasons.saa-ini-033:option:2: The CloudWatch Monitor METRICS and logs — does not detect threats with threat intelligence.
optionReasons.saa-ini-033:option:3: The WAF filter web requests — does not analyze account behavior.

finalJustifications: Because GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs with ML and threat intelligence, generating finding without installing agents.
Because GuardDuty automatically blocks detected malicious IPs, cutting communication before leaking.
Because GuardDuty installs light sensors in each instance EC2 of the account, capturing the traffic that logs do not record.
Because GuardDuty is the paid version of CloudTrail: the same events of API, increased real-time alerts.

optionReasons.saa-ini-112:option:0: Additional AZs do not increase the VPC in itself — sub-networks and VPC do not charge for AZ.
optionReasons.saa-ini-112:option:2: Sub-networks in an AZ receive internet traffic normally — resilience is the problem, not connectivity.
optionReasons.saa-ini-112:option:3: The Auto Scaling FUNCIONA with an AZ — only resilience is compromised.

finalJustifications: Because with everything in one AZ, her fall leads to the application INTEIRA together — single fault point that resilient architecture exists to avoid.
Because a single AZ limits the account to 20 instances, ceiling insufficient to absorb peaks of application.
Because the AWS does not offer SLA for resources implemented in a single AZ, leaving the application without contractual guarantee.
Because subnets of a single AZ cannot be registered in a Load Balancer, preventing traffic distribution.

optionReasons.saa-ini-115:option:0: Concentrate TUDO in the AZ of NAT gets worse: in addition to the internet, the whole application depends on an AZ.
optionReasons.saa-ini-115:option:1: Several NATs in MESMA AZ maintain the dependence of that AZ — its failure knocks down everyone.
optionReasons.saa-ini-115:option:3: Internet Gateway does not replace NAT for sub-networks PRIVADAS — would require public IPs and display entry.

finalJustifications: Because one NAT Gateway POR AZ, with each private subnet routing to NAT local, eliminates cross-dependence: failure of an AZ affects only its sub-networks.
Because three NAT Gateways triple the available output band, eliminating the gorgalo that knocked down the other two AZs.
Because NAT by AZ synchronizes the active connections between the zones, allowing the transparent failure of the open sessions.
Because NAT by AZ is mandatory by AWS from two private sub-networks — the current configuration violates the default.
